summary: Burundi is a small landlocked country in East Africa, on the northeastern shore of Lake Tanganyika, which became independent from Belgium in 1962 and moved its political capital from Bujumbura to Gitega in 2019.

ranking.name: Catholicism
ranking.description: Catholicism entered Burundi with German colonization at the end of the 19th century, and in 1898 missionaries of the White Fathers established the first mission station. After World War I Belgium took over (from 1923 as a League of Nations trust territory), and the Belgian colonial authorities cooperated closely with the Catholic Church, training a Tutsi elite through church schools; from the 1930s large numbers of chiefs and ordinary people were baptized, so Catholicism quickly became the majority religion.

ranking.name: Protestantism
ranking.description: Protestantism was introduced during the Belgian trusteeship by British, American and Scandinavian missions; for example the Anglican, Baptist and Methodist churches set up schools and hospitals in the east and north. After the civil war of 1993-2005, Pentecostal and independent evangelical churches grew rapidly in cities and among communities of returning refugees, and their share has risen to about one quarter.

ranking.name: Traditional beliefs and others
ranking.description: Traditional belief centers on the creator god Imana and also reveres ancestral spirits and the hero deity Kiranga. In the colonial period the Christian churches borrowed Imana as the translation for 'God', so that many people kept traditional ideas while converting to Christianity, and those who follow purely traditional religion are only a minority.

ranking.name: Islam
ranking.description: Islam was brought in the 19th century by Swahili and Arab merchants from the East African coast along Lake Tanganyika, and is concentrated mainly in the capital Bujumbura and lakeside commercial towns such as Rumonge. Because it arrived relatively late and was limited to merchant communities, Muslims make up only about 3 percent.

religion.background: Before colonization Burundi was a kingdom centered on a king (the mwami); its religion was mainly the creator god Imana and ancestor worship, and the king also had a religious role. After German colonization and Catholic missionaries entered at the end of the 19th century, Christianity spread rapidly, and during the Belgian trusteeship the church controlled the education system. After independence in 1962 the country experienced several episodes of ethnic violence between Hutu and Tutsi, and the churches played an important role in reconciliation. Today Burundi is a predominantly Christian country, but traditional ideas remain deeply rooted in everyday life.

language.official: Kirundi, French and English are the official languages.

ranking.name: Kirundi
ranking.description: Kirundi is a Bantu language close to Kinyarwanda; almost all Burundians, whether Hutu or Tutsi, speak it as a mother tongue, which is quite rare among African countries. It was the common language of the whole country in the kingdom era, was made the national language after independence, was made an official language in the 2005 constitution, and primary education is conducted in Kirundi.

ranking.name: Swahili
ranking.description: Swahili is the common trading language of East Africa; in the 19th century it was brought along Lake Tanganyika by merchants from the Tanzanian coast, and is spoken mainly in the commercial circles and Muslim communities of the capital Bujumbura and the lakeside towns. After Burundi joined the East African Community, the status of Swahili in schools has also gradually risen.

ranking.name: French
ranking.description: French became the language of administration and education during Belgian rule in 1916-1962, and after independence it remained the main language of government and higher education. But because only those with secondary education or above are fluent in French, only about 1 percent have it as a mother tongue. In 2014 English was also made an official language, in line with regional integration in the East African Community.

language.history: Before colonization Burundi was a unified kingdom in which Kirundi was spoken throughout the country, making it one of the few African countries with a highly unified language. It was colonized by Germany in the 1890s and taken over by Belgium after World War I, when French became the language of administration and education, while colonial education ran Kirundi and French in parallel. After independence in 1962, Kirundi and French were both official languages. In 2007 Burundi joined the East African Community, where English and Swahili predominate, and in 2014 English was also made an official language, and schools began to strengthen the teaching of English and Swahili.

ranking.name: Ugali
ranking.description: A thick, lumpy staple made by stirring cornmeal (or cassava flour) into water and cooking it; a small piece is pinched off by hand and dipped into stew or sauce.
ranking.history: Maize is native to the Americas and was brought to Africa by the Portuguese after the 16th century, becoming widespread as a staple on the East African plateau only in the 19th and 20th centuries; the name 'ugali' is used generally across the Swahili-speaking world of East Africa. In Burundi, an agricultural landlocked country, ugali is the basic daily meal for many families, and together with beans forms the main source of calories.

ranking.name: Cassava Leaf Stew
ranking.description: Pounded cassava leaves are stewed for a long time with palm oil, peanut butter, onion or small dried fish into a green stew with a thick texture, often eaten with ugali.
ranking.history: Cassava was promoted for planting during the colonial period because it tolerates drought, in order to prevent famine, and cassava leaves therefore became a common source of vegetables in the Great Lakes region. This dish is common in Burundi, Rwanda and eastern Congo, with similar names and methods. Because cassava leaves are cheap and rich in protein, it is an important source of nutrition in the daily diet of ordinary households.

ranking.name: Brochettes
ranking.description: Pieces of goat meat, beef or fish are threaded onto skewers, grilled over charcoal and sprinkled with salt, often served with fried plantain or fries; it is a popular snack at bars and roadside stalls.
ranking.history: 'Brochette' is French for 'skewer', and the name reflects the French influence left by Belgian colonial rule. Brochettes became part of urban bar culture after independence in the 1960s, and people often eat grilled goat skewers after work with local beer (such as Primus). Because goats are commonly raised in Burundian villages, goat skewers are the most common.

ranking.name: Ndagala
ranking.description: Small silvery fish from Lake Tanganyika, usually sun-dried and then fried or stewed with tomato and onion, eaten with ugali or rice.
ranking.history: Ndagala are small fish unique to Lake Tanganyika; the fishermen of the lake region traditionally attract them at night with lamps and then dry them in the sun on the lakeshore. Lake Tanganyika is the second deepest lake in the world, and its fishing sustains the inhabitants of lakeshore towns such as Bujumbura. Dried ndagala are easy to preserve and transport and are sold in the inland mountain regions, making them one of the most affordable sources of protein for Burundians.

ranking.name: Banana Stew
ranking.description: Unripe green cooking bananas are peeled and stewed with tomato, onion, beans or meat; the texture is soft like potato, and the taste is mild with a salty savoriness.
ranking.history: Bananas are generally thought to have come to East Africa from Southeast Asia through Indian Ocean trade more than a thousand years ago, and in the highlands of the Great Lakes region many cooking varieties developed, becoming an important staple. In Burundi, bananas are also used to brew traditional banana beer (urwarwa), which is shared at weddings and family gatherings. Stewed bananas are an important part of the daily diet and, paired with beans, provide the main nutrition.
